record.paper_title: Open Problems on Information and Feedback Controlled Systems
record.original_question: For feedback-controlled flashing ratchets, in which a controller uses information about the system state to rectify thermal fluctuations of Brownian particles by switching a periodic potential on and off, can the general entropy-reduction and thermodynamic results for feedback-controlled systems be applied to establish bounds on attainable entropy reduction and a thermodynamic description of these ratchets?

evidence.quote: a controller with information of the state of the system rectifies the thermal fluctuations of Brownian particles by switching on and off a periodic potential
The application of the results of [13] to feedback controlled flashing ratchets has not been done yet.
It will allow to establish bounds on the entropy reduction attainable for feedback flashing ratchet and to establish the thermodynamics of these systems

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a feedback-controlled flashing ratchet: an overdamped Brownian particle moves on the real line subject to thermal noise at temperature T and to a spatially periodic, asymmetric potential V(x) that a controller can switch on and off in time. At regular time intervals the controller measures the particle position (or some functional of the state) and, based on this information, decides whether the potential should be on or off during the next interval, with the goal of rectifying thermal fluctuations into directed motion.

Let S denote the Shannon/Gibbs entropy of the controlled stochastic process and let I denote the information acquired by the controller about the system state per unit time (or per control step). For a general class of feedback-controlled stochastic systems, one has a generalized second law of the form

    ΔS_total ≥ −I,

so that the information gathered by the controller permits an effective entropy reduction of the controlled system bounded by the acquired information, and a consistent thermodynamic description (work, heat, free energy, efficiency) can be formulated that incorporates this informational term.

Problem. Apply such general entropy-reduction and thermodynamic identities for feedback-controlled systems to the feedback flashing ratchet described above in order to:

(a) derive explicit, tight bounds on the entropy reduction attainable by the controller in terms of the information it acquires about the particle's state;

(b) establish a complete thermodynamic description of the feedback flashing ratchet — including expressions and bounds for the average current, extracted power, dissipated heat, and efficiency — that consistently incorporates the informational contribution and reduces to standard stochastic thermodynamics in the absence of feedback.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work has substantially addressed this program. A 2016 study established efficiency-at-maximum-power bounds for a discrete feedback ratchet, and a 2023 paper ("Information in feedback ratchets", Phys. Rev. E 108, 034112) computed the information from the entropy of the non-Markovian control sequence and proved that the maximum power and the power gain over open-loop operation are upper bounded linearly in the information. A 2024 work provides a Markovian description applicable to the feedback flashing ratchet. Thus explicit information-theoretic thermodynamic bounds and a thermodynamic description have been obtained, although fully general tight bounds for continuous, non-Markovian feedback ratchets remain an active topic.

status_evidence.title: Information in feedback ratchets
status_evidence.snippet: The maximum power output has an upper bound proportional to the information; the power-output increase from open-loop to closed-loop ratchet is also upper bounded linearly in the information.
status_evidence.claim: Tight information-based bounds on entropy reduction and power for the feedback flashing ratchet have been derived.

status_evidence.title: Efficiency at maximum power of a discrete feedback ratchet
status_evidence.snippet: Upper bound computed for the efficiency of an isothermal feedback ratchet at maximum power output.
status_evidence.claim: Efficiency bounds for feedback ratchets have been established.

status_evidence.title: Markovian description of a wide class of feedback-controlled systems: application to the feedback flashing ratchet
status_evidence.snippet: Provides a Markovian thermodynamic description applicable to the feedback flashing ratchet.
status_evidence.claim: A thermodynamic description of feedback flashing ratchets has been developed.
